mathcounts-potw-2026-09-07-01.prompt: Students at Sandstone Middle School have been welcomed back for the new school year. But it took Mr. Allen weeks to get all the classrooms ready. There are three classrooms along one hallway. The length and width of the classrooms increase proportionally. The 1st classroom measures 15 feet long by 18 feet wide. The 2nd classroom measures $18\frac34$ feet long by $22\frac12$ feet wide. The 3rd classroom is larger than the 2nd classroom. How many square feet of tile did Mr. Allen need to tile the floors in all three classrooms? Express your answer as a mixed number in simplest form.

mathcounts-potw-2026-09-07-02.prompt: Mr. Allen is getting three classrooms along one hallway ready for the school year. The length and width of the classrooms increase proportionally: the 1st classroom measures 15 feet long by 18 feet wide, the 2nd classroom measures $18\frac34$ feet long by $22\frac12$ feet wide, and the 3rd classroom is larger than the 2nd, enlarged by the same scale factor. The height of each classroom is 10 feet. Each classroom has a doorway that is $6\frac34$ feet tall and $3\frac12$ feet wide and a window that is 5 feet tall and $11\frac12$ feet wide. He paints the walls (not the floors or ceilings), except the doorways and windows. How many square feet did Mr. Allen have to paint in all three classrooms? Express your answer as a mixed number in simplest form.

mathcounts-potw-2026-09-07-03.prompt: Mr. Allen is getting three classrooms along one hallway ready for the school year. The length and width of the classrooms increase proportionally: the 1st classroom measures 15 feet long by 18 feet wide, the 2nd classroom measures $18\frac34$ feet long by $22\frac12$ feet wide, and the 3rd classroom is larger than the 2nd, enlarged by the same scale factor. The height of each classroom is 10 feet. Each classroom has a doorway that is $6\frac34$ feet tall and $3\frac12$ feet wide and a window that is 5 feet tall and $11\frac12$ feet wide. He paints the walls (not the floors or ceilings), except the doorways and windows. Mr. Allen tiles the floors of all three classrooms and paints the walls. When he only lays tile, Mr. Allen can lay 225 square feet of tile a day. When he only paints, Mr. Allen can paint 750 square feet a day. How many days did it take him to tile and paint all three classrooms? Express your answer to the nearest whole number.
